newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Buying mood keeps prices up on Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Buying mood keeps prices up on Bucharest bourse.

text.p: Strong buying interest drove stock prices higher on the Bucharest bourse on Thursday with traders expecting the bullish mood to continue in the first session next week.
Turnover slid to 85.15 million lei from Tuesday's 93.59 million with investors focusing on fertiliser maker Azomures SA, who took over 80 percent of turnover.
Brokers said bullish sentiment on the bourse was prompted by a depreciation in the local leu currency, which shed some 20 percent to 4,950/5,050 to the dollar from January 1.
"If the leu goes further down, prices will soar, if not, a profit-taking might show up any time," one trader said.
Brokers also said profit-taking might be spurred if any preliminary announcements of the 1996 financial results leaked from companies before March, when they are due.
On Thursday, thirteen stocks moved up, two closed weaker, one flat. Private syringe maker Sanevit SA remained suspended pending an announcement.
Two unofficial indices - the VAB, computed by Vanguard SA and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG -- rose by 5.0 percent and 4.97 percent from the previous session.
